bottom_line: In SHIFT, ivabradine vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82 [0.75–0.90]).
implications: These data support that, in SHIFT, ivabradine (vs placebo) lowered the risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90) and reduced hospital admission for worsening heart failure (16% vs 21%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66–0.83), while not demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–1.02; p = 0.092).

major_points.text: SHIFT was a multinational, event-driven, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in symptomatic chronic heart failure with LV systolic dysfunction.
major_points.quote: SHIFT was designed as a multinational, event-driven, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial including patients with moderate to severe heart failure and left-ventricular systolic dysfunction [14].

major_points.text: Eligibility included stable symptomatic chronic heart failure with LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, resting heart rate ≥70 bpm, and prior heart-failure hospitalization within 12 months.
major_points.quote: A total of 6558 adults with stable but symptomatic chronic heart failure (left-ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≤35%), a resting heart rate ≥70 bpm in sinus-rhythm, and admission to hospital for decompensated heart failure within the previous 12 months were included and randomised.

major_points.text: The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary composite endpoint was cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure.

major_points.text: A total of 6558 patients were randomised; 6505 were analysed after a mean follow-up of 23 months.
major_points.quote: A total of 6558 patients were randomised and 6505 patients were analysed after a mean follow-up of 23 months.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint events occurred in 24% with ivabradine vs 29% with placebo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90; p<0.0001).
Hospital admission for worsening heart failure was reduced (16% vs 21%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66–0.83; p<0.0001).
major_points.quote: Hospital admission for worsening heart failure 514 (16%) 672 (21%) 0.74 (0.66–0.83) <0.0001

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was not statistically significant (16% vs 17%; HR 0.90, 0.80–1.02; p=0.092).
Bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred more often with ivabradine (1% vs <1%).
major_points.quote: bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred in 48 patients (1%) taking ivabradine, compared to 10 patients (<1%) receiving placebo [14].

absolute_effects.text: Cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure: 793 (24%) vs 937 (29%).
Hospital admission for worsening heart failure: 514 (16%) vs 672 (21%).

subgroups.text: Pre-specified first secondary endpoint evaluated the primary composite in patients receiving at least 50% of the target daily dose of a beta-blocker at randomisation.
subgroups.quote: The pre- specified, first secondary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsen- ing heart failure in patients receiving at least 50% of the target daily dose of a beta-blocker (as defined by the European Society of Cardiology guidelines) at ran- domisation [14, 48].

subgroups.text: In the subgroup receiving at least 50% of the evidence-based target daily dose of a beta-blocker, the primary endpoint was not achieved (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.77–1.04; p=0.155).
subgroups.quote: in the subgroup of pa- tients receiving at least 50% of the evidence-based tar- get daily dose of a beta-blocker, the primary endpoint was not achieved (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.77–1.04, p = 0.155).

harms.text: Fewer serious adverse events occurred with ivabradine than placebo (45% vs 48%; p=0.025).
harms.quote: Overall, fewer seri- ous adverse events occurred in the ivabradine group (45% vs 48% in the placebo group, respectively, p = 0.025).

harms.text: Bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred in 48 (1%) with ivabradine vs 10 (<1%) with placebo.
harms.quote: bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred in 48 patients (1%) taking ivabradine, compared to 10 patients (<1%) receiving placebo [14].

harms.text: Visual disturbances occurred in 3% with ivabradine vs <1% with placebo.
harms.quote: in SHIFT, visual disturbances occurred in 89 patients (3%) randomised to ivabradine versus 17 patients (<1%) receiving placebo [14].

criticisms.text: The lack of benefit on all-cause mortality is noted as disappointing.
criticisms.quote: The lack of benefit on all-cause mortality is certainly disappointing.

criticisms.text: A very low use of device therapy in SHIFT was noted, despite guideline qualification.
criticisms.quote: Surprisingly, a very low use of device therapy in heart failure patients was noted. According to clinical guidelines, all patients in SHIFT would have qualified for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD), but in fact only 3% of the patients received such a device

criticisms.text: Recruitment strategy may have affected device-use patterns: most patients were recruited in eastern Europe with no centres in the USA.
criticisms.quote: This is likely to be related to the recruitment strategy in SHIFT: Two thirds of the patients were recruited in eastern Europe (66%) with no centres in the USA, and only 14% of the patients originated from western Europe [14].

criticisms.text: It is questioned whether patients were already on maximal tolerated beta-blocker dosages.
criticisms.quote: It is therefore questionable, if the patients were already on maximal toler- ated beta-blocker dosages.

criticisms.text: SHIFT was not designed to show an improvement in all-cause mortality (powered for composite primary endpoint).
criticisms.quote: However, SHIFT was not designed to show an improvement in all-cause mortality, since the study was powered for the compos- ite primary endpoint of cardiovascular death or hospi- talisation for worsening heart failure.

criticisms.text: Results of SHIFT are stated as questionable in NYHA functional class I or IV patients.
criticisms.quote: the results of SHIFT are questionable in patients in NYHA func- tional class I or IV.
